page: Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev5 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, featuring 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core performance, with high scores in multi-threaded stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core workloads. Memory performance is highly competitive, demonstrating strong uncached large-block read and write bandwidths of 286.33 GB/sec and 130.34 GB/sec respectively. It also exhibits strong performance in database operations, static web serving throughput, and multi-threaded decompression. However, single-core CPU benchmarks and LLM inference tasks, particularly text generation with large 70B models, fall into average or weak performance tiers.

Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the E64_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The absence of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive enterprise applications, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
